results.title: Formulas of linear temporal logic
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: For a type $A$ of atoms, the formulas of linear temporal logic (LTL) over $A$ are generated inductively: every atom $a \in A$ is a formula, the truth constant $\top$ is a formula, and if $\varphi$ and $\psi$ are formulas then so are the negation $\neg\varphi$, the conjunction $\varphi \wedge \psi$, the next formula $\mathbf{X}\,\varphi$ and the until formula $\varphi \mathbin{\mathbf{U}} \psi$.

results.title: Falsity in LTL
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The LTL formula $\bot$ (falsity) is defined as $\neg\top$, the negation of the truth constant $\top$.

results.title: Disjunction in LTL
results.caption: Definition
results.summary:
For LTL formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, the disjunction $\varphi \vee \psi$ is defined as $

results.title: Implication in LTL
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For LTL formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, the implication $\varphi \to \psi$ is defined as the disjunction $\neg\varphi \vee \psi$.

results.title: Bi-implication in LTL
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For LTL formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, the bi-implication $\varphi \leftrightarrow \psi$ is defined as the conjunction $(\varphi \to \psi) \wedge (\psi \to \varphi)$ of the two implications.

results.title: The eventually operator of LTL
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an LTL formula $\varphi$, the formula $\mathbf{F}\,\varphi$ ("eventually $\varphi$") is defined as the until formula $\top \mathbin{\mathbf{U}} \varphi$.

results.title: The always operator of LTL
results.caption: Definition
results.summary:
For an LTL formula $\varphi$, the formula $\mathbf{G}\,\varphi$ ("always $\varphi$") is defined as $
eg\,\mathbf{F}\,
eg\varphi$, the negation of "eventually $
eg\varphi$".

results.title: The release operator of LTL
results.caption: Definition
results.summary:
For LTL formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, the release formula $\varphi \mathbin{\mathbf{R}} \psi$ is defined as $
eg(
eg\varphi \mathbin{\mathbf{U}} 
eg\psi)$, the dual of until.

results.title: Satisfaction of LTL formulas on ω-words
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $v$ be a valuation that says which atoms are true at each letter, and for an ω-word $w$ and a natural number $k$ let $w^{(k)}$ be the suffix $i \mapsto w(k + i)$. Whether $w$ satisfies an LTL formula $\varphi$ under $v$, written $w \models \varphi$, is defined by recursion on $\varphi$: an atom $a$ holds when $v$ makes $a$ true at the first letter $w(0)$; truth always holds; $\neg \varphi$ holds when $\varphi$…

results.title: Satisfaction at a position
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $v$ be a valuation of atoms on letters, $w$ an ω-word, $k$ a natural number and $\varphi$ an LTL formula. Then $\varphi$ holds at position $k$ of $w$ under $v$ when the suffix of $w$ starting at position $k$, the ω-word $i \mapsto w(k + i)$, satisfies $\varphi$ under $v$.

results.title: Language of an LTL formula
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a valuation $v$ of atoms on letters, the ω-language of an LTL formula $\varphi$ is the set of ω-words that satisfy $\varphi$ under $v$.

results.title: Satisfaction at position zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every valuation of atoms on letters, ω-word $w$ and LTL formula $\varphi$, $\varphi$ holds at position $0$ of $w$ if and only if $w$ satisfies $\varphi$.

results.title: Satisfaction on a suffix
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $w$ be an ω-word and, for a natural number $k$, let $w^{(k)}$ be its suffix starting at position $k$, the ω-word $i \mapsto w(k + i)$. For every valuation of atoms on letters, every LTL formula $\varphi$ and every natural number $j$, $\varphi$ holds at position $j$ of $w^{(k)}$ if and only if $\varphi$ holds at position $k + j$ of $w$.

results.title: Satisfaction of an atom
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every valuation $v$ of atoms on letters, every ω-word $w$ and every atom $a$, the word $w$ satisfies the atomic formula $a$ under $v$ if and only if $v$ makes $a$ true at the first letter $w_0$ of $w$.

results.title: Falsity is never satisfied
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every valuation $v$ of atoms on letters and every ω-word $w$, the word $w$ does not satisfy the LTL formula $\bot$ (falsity) under $v$.

results.title: Semantics of eventually
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every valuation $v$ of atoms on letters, every ω-word $w$ and every LTL formula $\varphi$, the word $w$ satisfies $\mathbf{F}\,\varphi$ (eventually $\varphi$) under $v$ if and only if for some $k \in \mathbb{N}$ the suffix of $w$ starting at position $k$ satisfies $\varphi$ under $v$.

results.title: Semantics of release
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a valuation of atoms on letters, an ω-word $w$ and LTL formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, $w$ satisfies $\varphi \mathbin{\mathsf{R}} \psi$ ($\varphi$ releases $\psi$) if and only if for every position $k$, either $\psi$ holds at position $k$ of $w$ or $\varphi$ holds at some position $j < k$ of $w$.

results.title: Next is self-dual
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every valuation $v$ of atoms on letters, every ω-word $w$ and every LTL formula $\varphi$, the word $w$ satisfies $\neg\mathbf{X}\,\varphi$ under $v$ if and only if it satisfies $\mathbf{X}\,\neg\varphi$ under $v$, where $\mathbf{X}$ is the next operator.

results.title: Expansion law for until
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every valuation of atoms on letters, ω-word $w$ and LTL formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, $w$ satisfies $\varphi \mathbin{\mathsf{U}} \psi$ ($\varphi$ until $\psi$) if and only if either $w$ satisfies $\psi$, or $w$ satisfies $\varphi$ and also satisfies $\mathsf{X}(\varphi \mathbin{\mathsf{U}} \psi)$, that is, next ($\varphi$ until $\psi$).

results.title: Expansion law for release
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every valuation $v$ of atoms on letters, every ω-word $w$ and all LTL formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, the word $w$ satisfies $\varphi \mathbin{\mathcal{R}} \psi$ ($\varphi$ releases $\psi$) under $v$ if and only if it satisfies $\psi$ and it satisfies $\varphi$ or $\mathbf{X}(\varphi \mathbin{\mathcal{R}} \psi)$, all under $v$, where $\mathbf{X}$ is the next operator.

results.title: Idempotence of always
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every valuation $v$ of atoms on letters, every ω-word $w$ and every LTL formula $\varphi$, the word $w$ satisfies $\mathbf{G}\,\mathbf{G}\,\varphi$ under $v$ if and only if it satisfies $\mathbf{G}\,\varphi$ under $v$, where $\mathbf{G}$ is the always operator.

results.title: Always eventually means infinitely often
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every valuation $v$ of atoms on letters, every ω-word $w$ and every LTL formula $\varphi$, the word $w$ satisfies $\mathbf{G}\,\mathbf{F}\,\varphi$ (always eventually $\varphi$) under $v$ if and only if there are infinitely many $k \in \mathbb{N}$ such that the suffix of $w$ starting at position $k$ satisfies $\varphi$ under $v$.

results.title: Eventually always means from some point on
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every valuation $v$ of atoms on letters, every ω-word $w$ and every LTL formula $\varphi$, the word $w$ satisfies $\mathbf{F}\,\mathbf{G}\,\varphi$ (eventually always $\varphi$) under $v$ if and only if there is $n \in \mathbb{N}$ such that for every $k \ge n$ the suffix of $w$ starting at position $k$ satisfies $\varphi$ under $v$.

results.title: Satisfaction of an atom at a position
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $v$ be a valuation of atoms on letters, $w$ an ω-word, $a$ an atom and $k$ a natural number. The atomic formula $a$ holds at position $k$ of $w$ under $v$ if and only if $v$ makes $a$ true at the letter $w(k)$.

results.title: Relabelling the letters of an ω-word
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $v$ be a valuation of atoms on letters of an alphabet $\Sigma$, let $f \colon \Sigma' \to \Sigma$ be a map, and let $w$ be an ω-word over $\Sigma'$. For every LTL formula $\varphi$, the relabelled word $i \mapsto f(w(i))$ satisfies $\varphi$ under $v$ if and only if $w$ satisfies $\varphi$ under the valuation that makes an atom $a$ true at a letter $s$ of $\Sigma'$ exactly when $v$ makes $a$ true at $f(s)$.

results.title: Membership in the language of a formula
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every valuation $v$ of atoms on letters, every ω-word $w$ and every LTL formula $\varphi$, the word $w$ belongs to the ω-language of $\varphi$ under $v$ if and only if $w$ satisfies $\varphi$ under $v$.

results.title: Baumslag's group
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: Baumslag's group is the one-relator group $B = \langle a, b \mid (bab^{-1})\, a\, (bab^{-1})^{-1} = a^2 \rangle$, the quotient of the free group on the two generators $a$ and $b$ by the normal subgroup generated by $(bab^{-1})\, a\, (bab^{-1})^{-1} a^{-2}$.

results.title: Kapovich's conjugacy separability question (Kourovka 19.41)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The assertion that for every natural number $n$ and every automorphism $\varphi$ of the free group $F_n$ of rank $n$, the semidirect product $F_n \rtimes_\varphi \mathbb{Z}$, in which $k \in \mathbb{Z}$ acts on $F_n$ by $\varphi^k$, is conjugacy separable.

results.title: Finite-rank free-by-cyclic groups are conjugacy separable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every automorphism $\varphi$ of the free group $F_n$ of rank $n$, the semidirect product $F_n \rtimes_\varphi \mathbb{Z}$, in which $k \in \mathbb{Z}$ acts on $F_n$ by $\varphi^k$, is conjugacy separable: any two of its elements whose images are conjugate in every quotient by a normal subgroup of finite index are conjugate.

results.title: Pisano period
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, the Pisano period $\pi(n)$ is the minimal period of the pair $(0, 1)$ under the Fibonacci step $(a, b) \mapsto (b, a + b)$ on $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$: the least $k \ge 1$ such that $k$ applications of the step map $(0, 1)$ back to $(0, 1)$, or $0$ if there is no such $k$ (as for $n = 0$, where $\mathbb{Z}/0\mathbb{Z} = \mathbb{Z}$).

results.title: The Pisano period of $F_n$ divides $2n$ for even $n$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F_n$ denote the $n$-th Fibonacci number and $\pi(m)$ the Pisano period of $m$. For every even natural number $n > 1$, $\pi(F_n)$ divides $2n$.

results.title: Sum of the first $p$ Fibonacci numbers modulo a prime $p$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p > 5$ be a prime, let $F_i$ denote the $i$-th Fibonacci number, with $F_1 = F_2 = 1$, and let $S = F_1 + F_2 + \dots + F_p$. If $p \equiv 1$ or $4 \pmod 5$, then $S$ leaves remainder $1$ on division by $p$; if $p \equiv 2$ or $3 \pmod 5$, then $S$ leaves remainder $p - 2$ on division by $p$; and in every case $p$ does not divide $S$.

results.title: Upper bound for sifted shifted primes divisible by a large prime
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Divisor-power sum with complex exponent
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a complex number $s$, $\sigma_s$ is the complex-valued arithmetic function with $\sigma_s(n) = \sum_{d \mid n} d^s$ for every natural number $n \ge 1$, where $d^s$ is the complex power, and $\sigma_s(0) = 0$.

results.title: Divisor-sum formula for the complex-exponent divisor sum
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$ and complex number $s$, the divisor-power sum $\sigma_s$ with complex exponent $s$ satisfies $\sigma_s(n) = \sum_{d \mid n} d^s$, the sum running over the positive divisors $d$ of $n$; for $n = 0$ the sum is empty, so $\sigma_s(0) = 0$.

results.title: The complex-exponent divisor sum at one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every complex number $s$, the divisor-power sum $\sigma_s(n) = \sum_{d \mid n} d^s$ with complex exponent $s$ satisfies $\sigma_s(1) = 1$.

results.title: The complex-exponent divisor sum at exponent zero counts divisors
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\sigma_s(n) = \sum_{d \mid n} d^s$ be the divisor-power sum with complex exponent $s$. For every natural number $n$, $\sigma_0(n)$ equals the number of positive divisors of $n$, with the convention that $0$ has no divisors, so that $\sigma_0(0) = 0$.

results.title: Natural exponents give the classical divisor function
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $k$ and $n$, the value at $n$ of the complex-exponent divisor sum $\sum_{d \mid n} d^s$ with $s = k$ equals the natural number $\sigma_k(n) = \sum_{d \mid n} d^k$, viewed as a complex number.

results.title: The variable $x$ of $K((x^{-1}))$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $K$ be a field. Formal Laurent series in $x^{-1}$ over $K$ are realized as Laurent series $\sum_n c_n X^n$ in $X = x^{-1}$, and the variable $x$ is the series $X^{-1}$, with coefficient $1$ at $X^{-1}$ and $0$ elsewhere.

results.summary: Let $K$ be a field. In $K((x^{-1}))$, the product of the variable $x$ and the series $x^{-1}$ (coefficient $1$ at $x^{-1}$ and $0$ elsewhere) is $1$.

results.title: Polynomials as Laurent series in the inverse variable
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $K$ be a field. The embedding $K[x] \to K((x^{-1}))$ is the $K$-algebra homomorphism that sends $x$ to the element $x$ of $K((x^{-1}))$, that is, it evaluates a polynomial at $x$.

results.title: The polynomial variable embeds as the Laurent variable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a field. The embedding $K[x] \to K((x^{-1}))$ sends the polynomial $x$ to the element $x$ of $K((x^{-1}))$.

results.title: Polynomial part of a Laurent series
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $K$ be a field and write a Laurent series $\alpha \in K((x^{-1}))$ as $\alpha = \sum_n c_n x^{-n}$. Its polynomial part is $[\alpha] = \sum_{n \le 0} c_n x^{-n}$, the sum of the terms in nonnegative powers of $x$.

results.title: Coefficients of the polynomial part of a Laurent series
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a field and write $\alpha \in K((x^{-1}))$ as $\alpha = \sum_n c_n x^{-n}$. For every integer $n$, the coefficient of $x^{-n}$ in the polynomial part $[\alpha]$ is $c_n$ if $n \le 0$ and $0$ if $n > 0$.

results.title: Polynomial parts of the variable and its inverse
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a field. In $K((x^{-1}))$ the polynomial part of $x$ is $x$, and the polynomial part of $x^{-1}$ is $0$.

results.title: Complete quotients of a Laurent series
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $K$ be a field and $\alpha \in K((x^{-1}))$. The complete quotients of the continued fraction expansion of $\alpha$ are $\alpha_0 = \alpha$ and $\alpha_{n+1} = (\alpha_n - [\alpha_n])^{-1}$ for $n \ge 0$, where $[\beta]$ is the polynomial part of $\beta$ and $0^{-1} = 0$. results.title: Partial quotients of a Laurent series
results.caption: Definition

results.title: First step of the continued fraction of a Laurent series
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a field and $\alpha \in K((x^{-1}))$. The partial quotient $b_0$ of $\alpha$ is its polynomial part $[\alpha]$, and the complete quotient $\alpha_1$ is $(\alpha - [\alpha])^{-1}$, where $0^{-1} = 0$.

results.title: Laurent series with bounded partial quotients
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $K$ be a field. A Laurent series $\alpha \in K((x^{-1}))$ with partial quotients $b_0, b_1, \dots$ has bounded partial quotients if there is an integer $B$ such that for every $n \ge 0$ and every integer $k > B$ the coefficient of $x^k$ in $b_n$ is zero, that is, every nonzero $b_n$ is a polynomial in $x$ of degree at most $B$.

results.title: Numerators of the convergents of a Laurent series
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $K$ be a field and let $\alpha \in K((x^{-1}))$ have partial quotients $b_0, b_1, \dots$. The numerators of the convergents of $\alpha$ are $P_{-1} = 1$, $P_0 = b_0$ and $P_{n+1} = b_{n+1} P_n + P_{n-1}$ for $n \ge 0$. The sequence is indexed with a shift of one: its term at $n \ge 0$ is $P_{n-1}$.

results.title: Denominators of the convergents
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $K$ be a field, let $\alpha \in K((x^{-1}))$ and let $b_0, b_1, \dots$ be its partial quotients. The denominators of the convergents of $\alpha$ are given by $Q_{-1} = 0$, $Q_0 = 1$ and $Q_{n+1} = b_{n+1} Q_n + Q_{n-1}$ for $n \ge 0$. They are indexed from $0$ here: the $k$-th term of the sequence is $Q_{k-1}$.

results.title: The convergent $P_1 / Q_1$ of a Laurent series
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a field and let $\alpha \in K((x^{-1}))$ have partial quotients $b_0, b_1, \dots$. Let $P_n$ and $Q_n$ be the numerators and denominators of its convergents, given by $P_{-1} = 1$, $Q_{-1} = 0$, $P_0 = b_0$, $Q_0 = 1$, $P_{n+1} = b_{n+1} P_n + P_{n-1}$ and $Q_{n+1} = b_{n+1} Q_n + Q_{n-1}$. Then $P_1 = b_1 b_0 + 1$ and $Q_1 = b_1$.

results.title: BANDWIDTH instances
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: An instance of BANDWIDTH is a triple $(n, E, K)$ of a natural number $n$ (the number of vertices), a list $E$ of ordered pairs of natural numbers (the edges) and a natural number $K$ (the bound).

results.title: Well-formed BANDWIDTH instances
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A BANDWIDTH instance $(n, E, K)$ is well formed when the list $E$ has no repeated entries and every pair $(u, v)$ in $E$ satisfies $u < n$, $v < n$ and $u \ne v$, and its reverse $(v, u)$ does not occur in $E$. Thus $E$ lists the edges of a loopless undirected graph on the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$, each edge exactly once.

results.title: BANDWIDTH feasibility
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A BANDWIDTH instance $(n, E, K)$ is feasible when there is an ordering of the numbers $0, \dots, n-1$ such that $|p(u) - p(v)| \le K$ for every pair $(u, v)$ in $E$, where $p(m)$ is the position of $m$ in the ordering, counting from $0$, and $p(m) = n$ when $m$ is not among $0, \dots, n-1$.

results.title: The BANDWIDTH decision problem
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: BANDWIDTH accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding of triples $(n, E, K)$ of a natural number, a list of pairs of natural numbers and a natural number, to a BANDWIDTH instance that is both well formed and feasible. Bitstrings that do not decode to such a triple are rejected.

results.title: BANDWIDTH is NP-complete
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The BANDWIDTH decision problem belongs to NP, and every decision problem in NP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to it.

results.summary: For a list of weighted edges on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the associated ordered directed graph enumerates its vertices as $0, 1, \dots, n-1$, and the outgoing neighbor list of a vertex $u$ is the list of targets of the edges of the list with source $u$, in the order in which they occur and with repetitions.

results.title: Vertices of a path
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a vertex $s$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and a list of weighted edges $e_1, \dots, e_k$ on these vertices, the vertices of the path from $s$ along this list are the list $s, t_1, \dots, t_k$, where $t_i$ is the target of $e_i$.

results.title: Bellman–Ford path weight
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The weight of a list of integer-weighted edges is the sum of the weights of its entries, an edge occurring several times being counted each time.

results.title: Weighted path in an edge list
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $E$ be a list of weighted directed edges on the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$. A list $P = (e_1, \dots, e_k)$ of weighted directed edges is a weighted path in $E$ from $s$ to $t$ when every $e_i$ belongs to $E$, the target of $e_i$ is the source of $e_{i+1}$ for every $i < k$, and either $k = 0$ and $s = t$, or $k \ge 1$, the source of $e_1$ is $s$ and the target of $e_k$ is $t$.

results.title: Edges of the weight-forgetting graph
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a list $E$ of weighted directed edges on the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$ and vertices $u$, $v$, the graph obtained from $E$ by forgetting weights has an edge from $u$ to $v$ if and only if some edge in $E$ has source $u$ and target $v$.

results.title: Tail of a weighted path
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a list of weighted directed edges on the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$ and let $s$ and $t$ be vertices. If the list consisting of an edge $e$ followed by a list $R$ of edges is a weighted path in $E$ from $s$ to $t$, then $R$ is a weighted path in $E$ from the target of $e$ to $t$.

results.title: Appending an edge to a weighted path
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a list of weighted directed edges on the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$ and let $s$, $m$ and $t$ be vertices. If $P$ is a weighted path in $E$ from $s$ to $m$ and $e$ is an edge belonging to $E$ with source $m$ and target $t$, then the list $P$ followed by $e$ is a weighted path in $E$ from $s$ to $t$.

results.title: Weight of a path with an edge appended
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every list $P$ of weighted directed edges on the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$ and every weighted directed edge $e$ on these vertices, the weight of the list $P$ followed by $e$ is the weight of $P$ plus the weight of $e$.

results.title: Weighted paths give walks of the same length
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a list of weighted directed edges on the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$ and let $s$ and $t$ be vertices. If a list $P$ of $k$ edges is a weighted path in $E$ from $s$ to $t$, then there is a walk of length $k$ from $s$ to $t$ in the directed graph obtained from $E$ by forgetting the weights.

results.title: Reachability by weighted paths
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a list of weighted edges on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and vertices $s$ and $t$, the vertex $t$ is reachable from $s$ in the directed graph obtained from the list by forgetting the weights if and only if there is a weighted path from $s$ to $t$ using edges of the list.

results.title: Reachable negative cycle witness
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: For a list of weighted edges on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and a source vertex $s$, a reachable negative cycle consists of a base vertex $b$, a weighted path $p$ from $s$ to $b$ using edges of the list whose vertices along $p$ from $s$ are pairwise distinct, and a nonempty weighted path $c$ from $b$ to $b$ using edges of the list whose edges have pairwise distinct sources and whose weight is negative.

results.title: Existence of a reachable negative cycle
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $E$ be a list of weighted directed edges on the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$ and $s$ a vertex. Then $E$ has a negative cycle reachable from $s$ when there is a reachable negative cycle witness for $E$ and $s$: a base vertex $b$, a weighted path in $E$ from $s$ to $b$ that visits no vertex twice, and a nonempty weighted path in $E$ from $b$ to $b$ whose edge sources are pairwise distinct and whose total weight is…

results.title: Bellman-Ford distance table
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: For a graph on the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$, the output of a successful Bellman-Ford run consists of a source vertex $s$, for every vertex a distance that is either an integer or $\infty$, and for every vertex an optional predecessor edge (a weighted directed edge, or none).

results.caption: Definition

The path to a vertex $t$ is built backwards from $t$: at a vertex $v \ne s$, take the recorded predecessor edge $e$ of $v$, put it in front of the edges collected so far, and continue from the source of $e$. results.title: Bellman-Ford cost counters
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: The cost of a Bellman-Ford run is a pair of natural numbers: the number of edge occurrences checked by relaxation passes, and the number of predecessor edges read or emitted while reconstructing a negative-cycle witness.

results.title: Total Bellman–Ford cost
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The total of a Bellman–Ford cost record is its number of edge relaxation checks plus its number of negative-cycle witness reconstruction steps.

results.title: Bellman–Ford result
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: For a list of weighted edges on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and a source vertex $s$, a Bellman–Ford result is either a distance record (a source vertex, an optional integer distance for each vertex and an optional predecessor edge for each vertex) or a reachable negative cycle witness for the list and $s$.

Bellman–Ford run on $E$ from $s$ starts with distance $d(s) = 0$ and $d(v) = \infty$ for every other vertex $v$, and makes $n - 1$ passes over $E$ followed by one final pass. results.title: Bellman-Ford succeeds exactly when no negative cycle is reachable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a list of integer-weighted directed edges on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and let $s$ be a vertex. Bellman-Ford run on $E$ from $s$ returns distances if and only if there is no negative cycle reachable from $s$, that is, no simple path from $s$ to a vertex $b$ together with a nonempty cycle through $b$ along edges of $E$ whose edge sources are pairwise distinct and whose total weight is negative.

results.title: Bellman-Ford reports a negative cycle exactly when one is reachable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a list of integer-weighted directed edges on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and let $s$ be a vertex. Bellman-Ford run on $E$ from $s$ returns a reachable negative cycle witness if and only if a negative cycle is reachable from $s$, that is, there are a simple path from $s$ to a vertex $b$ and a nonempty cycle through $b$ along edges of $E$ whose edge sources are pairwise distinct and whose total weight…

results.title: Bellman-Ford distances are realized by walks
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a list of integer-weighted directed edges on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and let $s$ be a vertex. If Bellman-Ford run on $E$ from $s$ returns distances $d$ and the distance $d(t)$ of a vertex $t$ is a finite integer $\delta$, then there is a walk from $s$ to $t$ along edges of $E$ whose total weight is $\delta$.

results.title: Bellman-Ford distances are lower bounds on walk weights
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a list of integer-weighted directed edges on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and let $s$ be a vertex. If Bellman-Ford run on $E$ from $s$ returns distances $d$, the distance $d(t)$ of a vertex $t$ is a finite integer $\delta$, and $P$ is a walk from $s$ to $t$ along edges of $E$ (vertices may repeat), then $\delta$ is at most the total weight of $P$.

results.title: Bellman-Ford leaves exactly the unreachable vertices at infinite distance
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a list of integer-weighted directed edges on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and let $s$ be a vertex. If Bellman-Ford run on $E$ from $s$ returns distances $d$, with $\infty$ marking a vertex that has no finite distance, then for every vertex $t$, $d(t) = \infty$ if and only if $t$ is not reachable from $s$ in the directed graph obtained from $E$ by forgetting the weights.

results.title: Bellman-Ford predecessor edges are tight
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a list of integer-weighted directed edges on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and let $s$ be a vertex. Suppose Bellman-Ford run on $E$ from $s$ returns distances $d$ together with predecessor edges, and the predecessor edge of a vertex $t$ is an edge $e$ from $u$ to $v$ of weight $w$. Then $e$ belongs to $E$, $v = t$, and $d(u)$ and $d(t)$ are both finite with $d(t) = d(u) + w$.

results.title: Bellman-Ford gives the source no predecessor
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a list of integer-weighted directed edges on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and let $s$ be a vertex. If Bellman-Ford run on $E$ from $s$ returns distances together with predecessor edges, then $s$ has no predecessor edge.

results.title: Relaxation checks of Bellman-Ford pass by pass
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every list $E$ of weighted edges on $n$ vertices and every source $s$, Bellman-Ford run on $E$ from $s$ charges exactly $(n - 1) \cdot |E| + |E|$ relaxation checks, where $|E|$ is the length of $E$.

results.title: Bellman-Ford makes exactly $n \cdot |E|$ relaxation checks
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every list $E$ of weighted edges on $n$ vertices and every source $s$, Bellman-Ford run on $E$ from $s$ charges exactly $n \cdot |E|$ relaxation checks, where $|E|$ is the length of $E$ counting repeated edges.

results.title: Bellman-Ford spends at most $3n$ witness steps
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every list $E$ of weighted edges on $n$ vertices and every source $s$, Bellman-Ford run on $E$ from $s$ charges at most $3n$ negative-cycle witness reconstruction steps.

results.title: Bellman-Ford spends no witness steps when it returns distances
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every list $E$ of weighted edges on $n$ vertices and every source $s$, if Bellman-Ford run on $E$ from $s$ returns distances rather than a negative cycle, then the run charges zero negative-cycle witness reconstruction steps.

results.title: Witness cost of a returned negative cycle
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every list $E$ of weighted edges on $n$ vertices and every source $s$, if Bellman-Ford run on $E$ from $s$ returns a reachable negative cycle whose cycle has $c$ edges and whose path from $s$ to the cycle has $q$ edges, then the run charges exactly $n + c + q$ negative-cycle witness reconstruction steps.

results.title: Bellman-Ford makes at most $4 n |E|$ counted steps
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every list $E$ of weighted edges on $n$ vertices and every source $s$, the total cost of Bellman-Ford run on $E$ from $s$ (its relaxation checks plus its negative-cycle witness reconstruction steps) is at most $4 \cdot n \cdot |E|$, where $|E|$ is the length of $E$.

results.title: Iterated successor
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a successor map $\mathrm{succ}$ on the nodes $0, \dots, n-1$, where $\mathrm{succ}(v)$ is either a node or undefined, the $k$-step jump from $v$ is the node reached by applying $\mathrm{succ}$ $k$ times starting at $v$, and is undefined if some step is undefined: the $0$-step jump from $v$ is $v$, and the $(k+1)$-step jump is $\mathrm{succ}$ of the $k$-step jump.

results.title: Terminating successor functions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A successor function $\mathrm{succ}$ on the nodes $0, \dots, n - 1$, mapping each node to its successor or to nothing, terminates when from every node $v$ the walk of $n$ steps along $\mathrm{succ}$ runs off the end, that is, there is no node $n$ steps down the list from $v$.

results.title: Rank of a node in a linked list
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\mathrm{succ}$ be a successor map on the nodes $0, \dots, n-1$ whose lists terminate. The rank of a node $v$ is the least $k$ such that following $\mathrm{succ}$ for $k + 1$ steps from $v$ runs off the end of the list, that is, the number of nodes after $v$ in its list.

results.title: The characteristic property of the rank
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathrm{succ}$ be a successor map on the nodes $0, \dots, n-1$ whose lists terminate. For every node $v$ and every $k \in \mathbb{N}$, following $\mathrm{succ}$ for $k$ steps from $v$ runs off the end of the list if and only if $k > \operatorname{rank}(v)$.

results.title: Rank decreases along jumps
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathrm{succ}$ be a successor map on the nodes $0, \dots, n-1$ whose lists terminate. If following $\mathrm{succ}$ for $a$ steps from a node $v$ reaches the node $u$, then $a \le \operatorname{rank}(v)$ and $\operatorname{rank}(u) = \operatorname{rank}(v) - a$.

results.title: Pointer-jumping state for list ranking
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A pointer-jumping state on the nodes $0, \dots, n - 1$ assigns to each node a pointer, which is either a node or empty (once it points past the end of the list), and a distance in $\mathbb{N}$, the distance covered by the pointer.

results.title: Initial state of pointer jumping
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a successor map $\mathrm{succ}$ on the nodes $0, \dots, n-1$, where $\mathrm{succ}(v)$ is either a node or undefined (at the end of a list), the initial pointer-jumping state gives each node $v$ the pointer $\mathrm{succ}(v)$ and the distance $0$ if $\mathrm{succ}(v)$ is undefined and $1$ otherwise.

results.title: One round of pointer jumping
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: In one parallel round, every node $v$ whose pointer is a node $u$ adds the distance of $u$ to its own distance and moves its pointer to the pointer of $u$ (undefined if that of $u$ is); a node whose pointer is undefined keeps its distance and its undefined pointer.

results.title: The list-ranking state after $t$ rounds
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a successor function $\mathrm{succ}$ on the nodes $0, \dots, n - 1$, the pointer-jumping state after $t$ rounds is defined by recursion on $t$: after $0$ rounds it is the initial state of $\mathrm{succ}$, and after $t + 1$ rounds it is one round of pointer jumping applied to the state after $t$ rounds.

results.title: After enough rounds, the distances are the ranks
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathrm{succ}$ be a successor map on the nodes $0, \dots, n-1$ whose lists terminate, and let $t$ be a natural number with $n \le 2^t$. Then after $t$ rounds of pointer jumping from the initial state, the distance of every node $v$ is the rank of $v$.

results.title: Tabulating a list-ranking state
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The tabulation of a pointer-jumping state $s$ on the nodes $0, \dots, n - 1$ is the pair of arrays of length $n$ whose entries at $v$ are the pointer and the distance of $v$ in $s$.

results.title: List-ranking rounds on arrays
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a successor function $\mathrm{succ}$ on the nodes $0, \dots, n - 1$ and $t \ge 0$, the arrays after $t$ rounds are a pair of arrays (pointers and distances) defined by recursion on $t$: after $0$ rounds they are the tabulation of the initial state of $\mathrm{succ}$, and after $t + 1$ rounds they are one round on arrays applied to the arrays after $t$ rounds.

results.title: List ranking by pointer jumping
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a successor map $\mathrm{succ}$ on the nodes $0, \dots, n-1$, list ranking by pointer jumping runs $\lceil \log_2 n \rceil$ rounds of pointer jumping on arrays, starting from the initial state, and returns the resulting array of distances, whose entry $v$ is the distance of node $v$.

results.title: Pointer jumping ranks every list in ⌈log₂ n⌉ rounds
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathrm{succ}$ be a successor map on the nodes $0, \dots, n-1$ whose lists terminate. Then for every node $v$, entry $v$ of the table returned by list ranking by pointer jumping, which runs $\lceil \log_2 n \rceil$ rounds, is the rank of $v$.

results.title: The value $k$ steps ahead
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $n$ nodes be linked into lists by a partial successor function, each node $u$ carrying a value $x_u$ in an additive monoid $M$. results.title: Segment sums
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $n$ nodes be linked into lists by a partial successor function, and let each node $v$ carry a value $x_v$ in an additive monoid $M$ (not necessarily commutative). For $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and a node $v$, the segment sum of length $k$ from $v$ is the sum, in list order, of the values of the first $k$ nodes of the list starting at $v$ (fewer if the list ends sooner); for $k = 0$ it is $0$.

results.title: Suffix sums
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $n$ nodes be linked into lists by a partial successor function, each node $v$ carrying a value $x_v$ in an additive monoid $M$. The suffix sum of a node $v$ is the segment sum of length $n$ from $v$: the sum, in list order, of the values of the first $n$ nodes of the list starting at $v$ (fewer if it ends sooner).

results.title: The characteristic property of suffix sums
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$ nodes be linked into lists by a partial successor function such that, starting from any node, $n$ steps run off the end of its list, and let each node $v$ carry a value $x_v$ in an additive monoid $M$. Then for every node $v$, the suffix sum of $v$ is $x_v$ plus the suffix sum of the successor of $v$, or just $x_v$ if $v$ has no successor.

results.title: List ranking is the special case of unit values
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$ nodes be linked into lists by a partial successor function such that, starting from any node, $n$ steps run off the end of its list. If every node has value $1 \in \mathbb{N}$, then the suffix sum of every node $v$ is $\operatorname{rank}(v) + 1$, where $\operatorname{rank}(v)$ is the number of nodes after $v$ in its list.

results.title: State of pointer jumping for suffix sums
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: For $n$ nodes and a type $M$, a state assigns to each node $v$ a pointer, which is either a node or none (past the end of the list), and an accumulated value in $M$. The accumulated value is meant to be the sum of the node values from $v$ up to, but not including, the pointer's target.

results.title: Initial state of pointer jumping for suffix sums
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given nodes $0, \dots, n-1$ with a partial successor function $\mathrm{succ}$ and values $x_v$ in an additive monoid $M$, the initial state gives each node $v$ the pointer $\mathrm{succ}(v)$ (undefined at the end of a list) and the sum $x_v$.

results.title: One round of pointer jumping for suffix sums
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a state in which each node $v$ has a pointer $p(v)$, either a node or undefined, and a sum $s(v)$ in an additive monoid $M$, one round produces a new state as follows. If $p(v)$ is undefined, the pointer of $v$ stays undefined and its sum stays $s(v)$. If $p(v) = u$, the new pointer of $v$ is $p(u)$ and its new sum is $s(v) + s(u)$, with $s(u)$ added on the right so that list order is kept.

results.title: State after $t$ rounds of pointer jumping for suffix sums
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a partial successor function $\mathrm{succ}$ on nodes $0, \dots, n-1$, values $x_v$ in an additive monoid $M$ and $t \in \mathbb{N}$, the state after $t$ rounds is obtained from the initial state (pointers $\mathrm{succ}(v)$, sums $x_v$) by applying one round of pointer jumping $t$ times.

results.title: One round of pointer jumping on arrays
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given an array $P$ of pointers (each a node among $0, \dots, n-1$ or undefined) and an array $S$ of sums in an additive monoid $M$, one round returns arrays $P'$ and $S'$ of length $n$ where, for each node $v$: if $P[v]$ is undefined, then $P'[v]$ is undefined and $S'[v] = S[v]$; if $P[v] = u$, then $P'[v] = P[u]$ and $S'[v] = S[v] + S[u]$. A read outside an array gives an undefined pointer or the sum $0$.

results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $a_1, \dots, a_n$ (the preceding piles) and $b$ (the last pile), the nim-sum $a_1 \oplus \cdots \oplus a_n \oplus b$ is $0$ if and only if $b = a_1 \oplus \cdots \oplus a_n$, where $\oplus$ is bitwise exclusive or and the nim-sum of no piles is $0$.
